stories.title: India’s September trade deficit rises to $30.21 bn despite 23% export growth
stories.summary: In September, India’s trade deficit widened to $30.21 billion, while export values increased 23% year‑on‑year, according to the Economic Times. The growth in exports was insufficient to offset the rise in imports, resulting in a larger overall deficit for the month.
stories.why: A widening deficit can put pressure on the rupee and may prompt policymakers to adjust trade or monetary measures.

stories.title: IMF applauds India’s GDP data revamp, says currency weakness not a policy failure
stories.summary: The International Monetary Fund praised India’s recent overhaul of its gross domestic product reporting framework. In its remarks, the IMF said that the current weakness in the rupee does not reflect a policy failure and noted that India is confronting an energy‑price shock while still maintaining strong economic fundamentals.
stories.why: RBI action on currency speculation can affect rupee volatility, hedging costs and foreign-exchange conditions for businesses and investors.

stories.title: US inflation exceeds expectations in September, fuel prices a key factor
stories.summary: Official data released show that inflation for the 12‑month period ending September was higher than analysts had forecast. The increase was largely attributed to rising gasoline prices, which have climbed after disruptions to Middle East energy supplies linked to the US‑Israel conflict with Iran. The report comes ahead of the U.S. midterm elections, where cost‑of‑living concerns dominate campaign discussions.
stories.why: Inflation data can shift expectations for central-bank interest rates, bond yields, borrowing costs and household purchasing power.
stories.previousTitle: US inflation rises more than expected
stories.previousSummary: US inflation rose by more than expected in the year to September, according to official figures, in the final data release before the midterm elections next month.
